headline: The Iceman cometh: Price wins a fourth Grand Slam
standfirst: Gerwyn Price beat Gian van Veen 16-11 in Wolverhampton for his first TV ranking title since 2021, and he is back up to world number three.
body: Five years is a long time to wait for a major. Gerwyn Price has just ended the drought, beating Gian van Veen 16-11 in the Grand Slam of Darts final to win the Eric Bristow Trophy for the fourth time, after 2018, 2019 and 2021.

It was level at 7-7 and tight as a drum. Then Price won the leg that mattered, taking out the last four from a long way back in 21 darts for 8-7, and the match tilted his way. Six legs in a row followed, with checkouts of 100, 60 and 40 along the way, and it was 13-7 before Van Veen could breathe. Price had finished 150 early on and 145 to rescue the middle of the match. When Van Veen pulled it back to 13-9, he answered with a 132. The 118 that closed it was the full stop.

The numbers say the doubles decided it. Price hit 53.3 per cent of his finishing attempts to Van Veen's 34.4, and averaged 97.34 against 94.76. That is a shade below Price's 12-month figure of 98.66, which tells you this was a title won with the finishing, not the scoring. Van Veen's highest checkout of the night was 80.
It was Van Veen's first Grand Slam final, and he leaves with £100,000. Price takes £200,000 and moves up to world number three, and he has now beaten the Dutchman 14 times in 17 meetings.

The wider tournament had plenty to say for itself too: 350 maximums, two nine-darters in the Van Gerwen and Sykes quarter-final, and three players on 170 checkouts. Yet the trophy went to the man who kept his head when the finals before this one had slipped away. Price said afterwards he wants "the big one at the end of the year".

Our view: the Grand Slam winner has gone on to World Championship glory in recent years, and Price knows it. With the Players Championship Finals starting in Minehead this Friday, he is the man everyone now has to worry about.
